summary.headline: HOEC Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rebounded to INR117.5 crore (from negative INR194 crore) on Kharsang volumes and $95.5/bbl crude, but PBT fell to INR12.5 crore.
summary.overview:
Standalone net revenue was INR107.6 crore against a prior quarter hit by the HPCL sale reversal, with Kharsang output rising from about 12,300 to 17,400 BOE and crude realisation near $95.5/bbl. Standalone PBT before exceptionals fell to INR12.5 crore from INR30.4 crore, and consolidated PBT to INR6.5 crore from INR9.01 crore, due to lower crude inventory offsets. B-80 output was hit by higher water cut, and HPCL-stored crude is being resold to third parties at a slower pace and at an expected loss of about 7-10%. Management is raising debt to fund the B-80 workover and three-well programme, with Dirok and PY-1 gas monetisation contingent on pipeline and gas-offtake milestones.</overview>

segments.name: B-80 (offshore, Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Output reduced by higher water cut in one well; compressor trains reconfigured to series and in test mode, with production partial but expected to reach full level by month-end. Two workovers (D1, D2) to start after rig mobilisation by October, and three new wells targeted by June 2027. Gas realisation about $16.5/MMBtu.

segments.name: Kharsang (Assam)
segments.commentary: Production rose from about 12,300 to 17,400 BOE QoQ after nine-well programme and workovers on 23 shut-in wells (five or six done). Second nine-well phase awaits rig award and tubulars in one to two months. Virgin gas found in two wells with no pipeline yet.

segments.name: Dirok (Assam)
segments.commentary: Operator with about 27% interest; production limited to 50-70% of well capability by evacuation constraints. DNPL line capacity degraded to about 1-1.5 MMSCMD versus 2.5 MMSCMD design; restoration via hot-tap work targeted by December. Gas realisation about $12.5/MMBtu.

segments.name: PY-1 (East Coast)
segments.commentary: Three wells suffered serious production loss; rig-less intervention contract awarded and funded from own books. Two new wells, earlier planned for Q4 FY28, now contingent on a take-or-pay gas agreement with GAIL or IOCL. Management cites 15-20 MMscfd potential from two new wells.

segments.name: Cambay (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Asjol, Balol and Palej assets; Palej debottlenecking gave 5-6% production increase QoQ, with 20-30% growth expected. Belt technology trial at Balol. New exploration block in final approval stage.

segments.name: B-15 (new block)
segments.commentary: 16 MMBOE reserves (to be reappraised); FDP under preparation with three or four concepts including tie-back to ONGC platform; drilling in FY28.

guidance_outlook: B-80 remaining crude inventory expected to be fully cleared from HPCL Chembur tanks by end-October or early November 2026; first small-tanker sale of about 120,000-130,000 bbl planned for October.

B-80 workovers: two wells to be on production by November-December 2026; three new wells by June 2027; per-well output 500-800 bbl/d (management range 8,900-13,000 bbl/d total in investor deck referenced by analyst; 1,000-1,500 bbl per well in simulation).
Dirok gas flow to the national grid targeted for December 2026, with DNPL capacity raised toward 2.5 MMSCMD; Kharsang pipeline targeted for completion around December 2027 (14-18 month build).
Cash flows expected to fund B-15 growth by November-December 2027; debt being raised for B-80 programme and pipelines.
Management indicated a 7-10% loss on HPCL crude sale (not guidance); INR4-7 crore losses already incurred on about 15% sold.
capex_capacity: B-80 programme (two workovers, three wells, jacket and production deck) to run as a single campaign; rig contract not yet awarded; capex contingency raised due to tight rig availability and drawdown on need basis.
Kharsang second phase of nine wells: rig identified, award imminent, tubulars ordering.
Kharsang pipeline: 24 km connection into Oil India line at Bordumsa; route survey tender closing, right of way expected in 6-8 months, build 6-8 months.
DNPL restoration: hot-tap work by Assam Gas Company Limited (16-20 week lead time) plus 100-200 m NRL-premises pipeline link; capacity to rise from about 1-1.5 MMSCMD to 2.5 MMSCMD at 90 bar.
Palej: additional new wells and sucker rod pumps ordered.
demand_pricing: Crude realisation of about $95.5/bbl standalone in Q1, up from $70.8/bbl, aided by favourable Brent.
B-80 gas traded on exchange at about $15-16/MMBtu; Dirok and PY-1 gas pegged at roughly $10-12/MMBtu per management.
HPCL crude: reversed sale in March-April 2026; crude now sold to third parties via tankers; Brent decline driving realisation losses.
Management said NRL can act as reseller and gas can be sold on exchange within about three days once a credible grid path exists.
Common carrier status for DNPL means other operators compete for capacity; HOEC's locked-in volumes are 0.5-0.7 MMSCMD gross.
